Creator's rebuttal: many hours of 'blood, sweat and tears' went into optimizing those skills, so deleting them is unacceptable
Creator's joke theory: the advice is a 'conspiracy' to make people use less usage so Anthropic saves money (no evidence offered)

relevance.why: Zero new information; the only substantive point is the stitched YC advice, which overlaps with the already-liked 'keep CLAUDE.md thin, replace NEVER rules with judgment' video. Entertainment for people who maintain skills/hooks, which Haji does.

implement_score.why: Not worth acting on from this clip. The underlying idea (periodically audit and prune CLAUDE.md/skills/hooks so they do not encode workarounds for old model weaknesses) is sound and cheap: a quarterly pass with /doctor and a review of each skill's purpose. But a wholesale delete is a bad fit for a time-poor founder; version them in git and prune instead.

verify: Who said this in the YC clip and what was the full reasoning (e.g. Claude 5 made most rules obsolete)?
Does Anthropic's own Claude 5 guidance (80% system-prompt cut, /doctor) actually recommend deleting vs. slimming?
Is the 'NEO NICHE.' brand the creator's own channel/product?

gap.what: Duplicate of liked content: the 'keep CLAUDE.md thin, skills on demand, run /doctor' video already covers the prune-your-config idea in more depth. Only new angle is the stronger 'delete everything every six months' framing from a YC speaker, with no argument given.
